scenes.stat_label: US SLOT REVENUE BEATS MOVIES + BASEBALL
bullets: U.S. slot machines took in $35.5B in 2023
Retail apps copied the same brain trigger
scenes.narration: In 2023, U.S. commercial casino slot machines took in thirty-five and a half billion dollars, several times the entire North American movie box office. The same mechanism is sitting inside your phone.
scenes.source: American Gaming Association, Commercial Gaming Revenue Tracker (2023)

scenes.headline: B.F. Skinner's Variable Ratio Discovery
bullets: Fixed schedule: pecking came in bursts with pauses
Random schedule: fast, steady pecking that was hard to stop
scenes.narration: In 1957, Charles Ferster and B.F. Skinner found that pigeons rewarded on a fixed schedule pecked in bursts, then paused. With rewards after an unpredictable number of pecks, they pecked fast and kept going.

scenes.headline: Uncertainty Keeps You Chasing
scenes.left_body: Pull-to-refresh feeds, spin-the-wheel coupons, flash timers
scenes.right_body: Delete saved cards -> type 16 digits manually -> wait 48 hours
scenes.narration: Brain research from Wolfram Schultz's lab found dopamine activity builds most when the odds of a reward are fifty-fifty. Flash-sale countdowns, mystery discounts, and pull-to-refresh feeds use that same uncertainty.

scenes.headline: Kill 1-Click Checkout Tonight
scenes.stat_subtext: Walking to grab your physical wallet breaks the impulse loop
scenes.narration: To disarm the algorithm, delete saved payment cards from every shopping app tonight. Walking across the room to type sixteen digits gives you time to change your mind.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
